A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KV-cache clustering research, with Chelsea renamed CentroidKV. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack evaluations, inference latency and memory measurements, and chunking/outlier-head ablations in Section 7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 reports original RULER and LongBench evaluations, compression ablations, latency and memory measurements, vLLM serving experiments, and bootstrap analyses in Section 6 and Appendices C–F.

M1.justification: V2 changes the cache budget from R(n+Gamma) to Rn and revises the prefill compression trigger. V1's offline outlier-head calibration and full-cache protection disappear from the described method. V2 also specifies a shared compression schedule instead of v1's model-specific capped schedules. Decreasing compression ratios already existed in v1 Appendix C.2; chunked matching and degree-weighted centroids remain.

E1.justification: V2 replaces the standalone Needle-in-a-Haystack evaluation with the broader 13-task RULER suite, including multiple-key/query/value retrieval, UUID scenarios, variable tracking, and word aggregation. LongBench coverage contracts from 21 datasets to 16, removing five Chinese datasets, including DuReader and MultiFieldQA-zh. WikiText-2 remains represented in the motivating observations.

E2.justification: CaM is removed from the reported comparisons and PyramidKV joins the main accuracy comparisons. StreamingLLM and SnapKV, already accuracy baselines in v1, newly participate in the main latency/memory comparisons. Appendix E additionally evaluates ClusterKV against its own dense-cache baseline and compares that efficiency profile with CentroidKV's.

E3.justification: Benchmark backbones change from Llama-2, Llama-3.1, and Qwen2 to Llama-3.1 and Mistral. The main reference cache budget changes from 20% to 25%, SnapKV's observation window changes from 100 to 64 tokens, and primary memory reporting changes from total GPU memory to KV-cache memory. New protocols include vLLM batch-one latency/peak throughput and FP16 comparisons with a fixed 2048-token cache.

E4.justification: V1's outlier-head calibration visualizations and protection ablations are removed. The chunking analysis changes from LongBench subsets and earlier latency settings to RULER accuracy with TTFT measurements through 128K contexts. V2 Table 9 adds a systematic sweep of initial compression ratios and decay rates, testing a schedule that v1 described but did not ablate.

E5.justification: V1 provides point estimates without comparable uncertainty reporting. V2 Appendix F introduces nonparametric bootstrap standard deviations across both benchmarks and models, selected numerical 95% percentile confidence intervals, and significance interpretations. Bootstrap resample counts and seeds are unspecified; these additions do not establish repeated independent model runs.

E6.justification: Accuracy and efficiency results are extensively replaced under changed settings. V1 reports up to 3.19× decoding and 2.72× end-to-end speedups; v2 reports up to 1.92× decoding speedup and 4.00× vLLM throughput gain. New results also expose losses: at 25% budget on Mistral LongBench, CentroidKV scores 28.56 versus SnapKV's 32.55 (Table 18). These are not same-setting cross-version regressions.

T1.justification: The balanced-partition optimization, convex decreasing score assumption, optimality theorem, and proof are retained: v1 Section 6 and Appendix A become v2 Appendix A. The attention approximation and complexity analysis also remain. Equation renumbering and correction of an obvious centroid subscript typo do not constitute new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the headline claims of 80% cache reduction, 3.19× decoding acceleration, and 2.72× end-to-end acceleration with 75% reduction, 1.92× decoding acceleration, and a new 4× serving-throughput claim. This materially revises the advertised efficiency contribution, while retaining the central clustering novelty and partition-optimality claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of UUID and exact/index-sensitive retrieval failures, contrasting semantic aggregation with precise token preservation. It discusses LongBench ties and deficits, attributes serving gains to freed memory and concurrency, and interprets equal-budget efficiency as comparable to other compression methods. V1 instead emphasized outlier-head necessity and broadly retained accuracy. The stated static-ratio limitation becomes a manually specified schedule limitation.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents KVPress, context/question separation, SnapKV's pooling kernel, PyramidKV's shape parameter, and vLLM cache write-back/block reclamation on a single A100. V1 does not establish whether questions were available during compression. Calibration details and model-specific settings are removed, while shared schedule parameters are supplied. Unlike v1 Appendix C.2, v2 does not specify a decay cap or positive-ratio safeguard.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting RULER, Mistral, KVPress, vLLM, FlashAttention, and bootstrapping, while dropping works including Squeezed Attention and Quest. Appendix E expands the distinction between already-cited ClusterKV's recall mechanism and centroid replacement. The central positioning as ToMe-inspired online KV-cache clustering remains.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming Chelsea to CentroidKV, v2 extensively rewrites the experimental narrative and interpretations, consolidates related-work discussion, and expands the inference/compression explanation. The standalone theoretical section moves into Appendix A, outlier-head sections disappear, and the appendices are reorganized around benchmark results, serving, ClusterKV, and statistics.

P2.justification: V1's individual-task performance panels, end-to-end bar chart, outlier heatmaps, and standalone retrieval heatmaps are replaced by aggregate RULER/LongBench curves and substantially reorganized result tables. V2 adds serving, ClusterKV, schedule-ablation, and uncertainty tables, reformats Algorithm 1, and adopts a different journal layout. The conceptual Figures 1–3 are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the accuracy–efficiency tradeoff more credible through broader equal-budget efficiency comparisons, vLLM serving measurements, explicit retrieval failures, and bootstrap uncertainty. These improve on v1's narrower efficiency comparisons and point estimates. The net gain is limited by reduced bilingual/model coverage, omission of v1's compression-schedule safeguards, and significance claims broader than the intervals actually reported.
